note.explanation: Base quantities are the chosen starting quantities. A derived quantity is described using one or more base quantities. Measurements compare an unknown quantity with a standard, and every measurement needs both a number and a unit.
examples: Distance and time are base quantities; speed depends on distance and time, so speed is derived.
Density is described in terms of mass and volume, so density is derived.
note.checkAnswer: Speed is derived because it depends on distance and time, which are base quantities.
note.simple: Base quantities are the starting quantities. Derived quantities are made from them. A measurement needs a number and a unit.

note.title: Base and Derived Quantities
steps: Check whether it is one of the chosen base quantities or is described using base quantities.
If it depends on one or more base quantities, call it a derived quantity.
For any measurement, include both the number and the unit.
note.answer: Base quantities are chosen quantities used as a starting point. Derived quantities are described in terms of one or more base quantities. A measurement is a comparison with a standard and consists of a number and a unit.

A quantity described using base quantities

mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes a base quantity?
rationales: Correct: the textbook says scientists selected some quantities to play a key role and called them base quantities.
This describes a derived quantity.
A measurement without a unit is meaningless; it is not a base quantity.
A standard for measuring time is not the definition of a base quantity.

options: A quantity described in terms of one or more base quantities
A quantity that cannot be measured
A quantity that has no unit

mcqs.stem: What is a derived physical quantity?
rationales: Correct: this is the textbook definition of derived physical quantities.
Derived quantities can be measured; this is not their definition.
Measurements of derived quantities also need units.
This describes the role of a standard in measurement, not a derived quantity.

options: A comparison of an unknown quantity with a widely accepted standard quantity

mcqs.stem: Which option gives the textbook definition of measurement?
rationales: Correct: measurement compares an unknown quantity with a widely accepted standard quantity.
The definition requires comparison with a standard, not merely with another unknown quantity.
A number without a unit does not make a meaningful measurement.
A unit needs to be a standard, not just any convenient object.

options: A number and a unit
A number and an instrument
A unit and a physical object
A standard and a physical object
mcqs.stem: What are the two parts of a measurement?
rationales: Correct: a measurement consists of a number and a unit.
An instrument may be used to measure, but it is not one of the two parts of the measurement.
A physical object is not a required part of the written measurement.
A standard is used for comparison but is not one of the two parts of the measurement.

options: It depends on distance and time

mcqs.stem: Why is speed a derived quantity?
rationales: Correct: the textbook says speed depends on distance and time, which are base quantities.
Speed is a quantity, not a standard unit.
This describes part of measurement, not why speed is derived.

options: A unit is a standard of measurement
A unit is the number in a measurement
A unit is an unknown quantity
A unit is a measuring instrument
mcqs.stem: What is a unit of measurement?
rationales: Correct: the textbook identifies the standard of measurement as a unit.
The number is the other part of a measurement.
A unit is a standard, not the unknown quantity being measured.
An instrument may help measure, but it is not the unit.

explain.title: Base quantities
explain.body: Scientists have selected arbitrarily some quantities to play a key role. They are called base quantities.

explain.title: Derived quantities
explain.body: All the quantities which can be described in terms of one or more base quantities are called derived physical quantities. For example, speed depends on distance and time, and density is described in terms of mass and volume.

explain.title: Measurement and units
explain.body: A measurement is a process of comparison of an unknown quantity with a widely accepted standard quantity. The standard of measurement is called a unit.

explain.title: Two parts of a measurement
explain.body: A measurement consists of two parts, a number and a unit. A measurement without unit is meaningless.

mistakes: Calling speed a base quantity instead of a derived quantity; speed depends on distance and time.
Giving examples without labelling which are base and which are derived.
Writing only a number for a measurement and leaving out its unit.
Saying a standard unit is needed only for convenience; explain that it helps different people obtain the same result and prevents confusion.
